summary: Steel tower from the Fort Lewis Rainier lookout, sold and removed around 2000, rebuilt by Sahale for IslandWood and dedicated as Canopy Tower in 2009; standing.

facts.design: 112-foot all-steel tower with a rebuilt cab, treads and an added ADA-compliant helical stairwell
facts.status_note: The original Rainier site tower is gone; this steel tower was dismantled, stored and rebuilt at IslandWood on Bainbridge Island

events.note: Sahale's page says the tower was erected at Fort Lewis in 1966; the register and firelookout.com give 1968
112-foot all-steel tower replaced the 1942 timber tower at the Rainier site, per the register and firelookout.com
Decommissioned and sold for scrap, per Sahale; the dismantled tower spent years in storage
Sold and removed from the Fort Lewis site, per firelookout.com; the register says sold, then moved to and sold again to IslandWood
Reconstruction at IslandWood completed February 2009 by Sahale LLC; the register says it was dedicated as Canopy Tower in May 2009

corrections.why: 125.0 looks like a feet figure written as metres (125 ft is 38.1 m). The rebuilder's page gives 118 ft for the tower as it stands today (36.0 m), and also gives 125 ft in its opening paragraph.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sahale dates the Fort Lewis erection to 1966; the register and firelookout.com date the 112-foot steel tower's replacement of the timber tower to 1968. Both dates are reported and neither is chosen.
Sahale gives 125 ft in its opening paragraph and 118 ft for the tower as it stands today. The record uses 118 ft (36.0 m) as the current height and notes the 125 ft figure.
Sahale says decommissioned in 1998; the register and firelookout.com say sold and removed in 2000. Both are kept as separate events.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 125.0 is a feet figure entered as metres; corrected to 36.0 m (118 ft, the rebuilder's 'stands today' figure). The same Sahale page also says 125 ft, so the current height is not settled. Built date conflicts (1966 Sahale vs 1968 register/firelookout.com) are both kept. Firm name: the cited page says Sahale LLC (Seattle Bridge Builders); the sibling record's 'Sahale Snowkites & Climbing' is not on that page and should not be reused. The FFLOS register entry US 559, WA 5 belongs to the gone Rainier Lookout Site record (us-wa-rainier), not this relocated tower. No staffing, fire history, or public-access information found in any page read; the sibling record reports the same gap. The Canopy Tower sits at IslandWood Environmental Learning Center; no access level set because the sources do not say whether the public can visit. Verification 2026-10-09: the story now attributes 'all-steel' only to firelookout.com (the register says 112' steel); the 1968 replacement sentence cites the register; the 3D model claim is tied to the Sahale page's reference to old plansets. Both 1966 and 1968 dates remain reported.
